comment:
Dr. Persaud is great! He is a very personable professor who wants to see you succeed.

Grading: 65% on 3 exams, 25% on problem sets, 10% on participation. Grading can be opaque and seemingly arbitrary, but clarified during office hours. Exams are only challenging due to their pace.

If you like ECON and are a solid test-taker, he's the man.

Micro 271 will always be one the hardest classes in the B School but Persaud is definitely the better professor. The 3 Tests are 60%, Problem Sets are 30%, and the rest is basically a free 100%. Problem sets are extremely hard but he grades leniently so ~90% is possible. His tests are hard but his final was IMPOSSIBLE. Ended with a B+ (Got blessed)

Dr. Persaud has been my favorite prof I've taken in college so far. He is understanding towards his students, and the grade distribution is great (problem sets are worth more than one exam). He is extremely accessible outside of class and explains new, challenging concepts clearly and in a way that is digestible. He's fantastic. TAKE HIM IF U CAN.

Dr. Persaud is probably the best Microtheory professor you'll find. Super personable and very accessible outside of class. His lectures are clear, engaging, and actually enjoyable. Problem sets and exams are application-based, so be ready to really understand the material—but he sets you up for success.

Dr. Persaud is one of my favorite professors. I highly recommend going to office hours because we go through the questions as a group and confirm that we have all the correct answers. He is super smart but also humble. Exams are difficult, but there are no tricks. Pay attention to random facts he says in class bc they might appear as extra credit.
Dr. Persaud is great. He's very smart, funny, and the lectures are great. The problem sets can be a huge pain in the ass but the exams aren't as bad. Take him for micro theory!

His problem sets are very difficult, but he knows this and makes it clear that the exams are not as hard. The problem sets are meant to challenge you. Use the course mentors and his office hours! I was terrified of this class before going in, but Dr. Persaud made it fun and allows so many chances for extra credit!

Dr. Persaud took one of the hardest classes that I had been dreading since I had to withdraw from it the previous semester and made it one of my favorites. He is funny and so patient, and was able to thoroughly explain difficult concepts in simple terms without patronizing. If you are dreading micro theory, I couldn't recommend Persaud enough!

Persaud makes a near impossible class very doable. Although the concepts can be very tricky (and problem sets are impossible), he is very understanding and will do anything to make sure his students get the best education they can. He won jeopardy a few times, so be ready for extra credit trivia questions. Very smart and funny

Dr. Persaud is a good professor overall as you can understand what he says and he provides help. However, he lacks empathy with his students by making extremely hard and lengthy exams that absolutely nobody can finish. Extra credits are trivia questions that only 1 student gets right (if so). His final exam is the most unfair test I've taken at UR.

Dr. Persaud is a great professor and actively collaborates with students. His class heavily relies on discussion and limited note-taking on the board (no slide presentations, study guides, or written notes provided), which may sometimes leave you feeling lost. His exams are difficult and the assignments will consume your entire weekend.

Dr. Persaud is an EXCELLENT professor. This is the first semester he is teaching ECON 271, and he is very good at responding to students' needs. He is also quite funny and EXTREMELY knowledgeable. I really appreciate how he always asks if we have questions before moving on to a new topic. Problem sets and exams are hard, start early

An amazing, thoughtful, and engaging professor. It is clear he takes time to prepare lectures with both structured content and relevant examples. His problem sets and exams are a little too difficult at times, but they make you understand the material at a deeper level. A little too much algebra that takes away from the economic concepts. Funny too

Honestly, a really great guy who puts a lot of effort into making sure his students get the material. Problem sets are hard, but he gives opportunities for extra credit and holds office hours very often. Keeps his class very structured and does his best to keep the class engaged and aware of why concepts are relevant to the field

People rate his class to be hard simply because he can't teach. Students are bored in his class and are confused by the lack of structure. Just throws in random examples here and there and expects students to get it.

He is a really nice guy and will meet with you always, but hardest class ever taken. Insanly long problem sets each week, it will take HOURS! This class is very HEAVY in Excel. Test were insane. I have never taken a test were I left everything blank before until then. Way to hard for Inro-BStats. Nice curve and I do like his teaching style.

Unlike some I liked Persaud. Genuinely nice guy whos kinda funny in a dorky way and a good teacher. Class is pretty hard though, the problem sets take 5-8 hours and are brutal. The tests aren't that bad and you get a notecard for all the equations. Overall if you grind on problem sets and pay attention you'll do fine even if you've never taken stat
The correlation between taking Dr. Persauds class and having your cheeks clapped have a correlation r value of 1.01.

This man is brutal. Gives ridiculously long problem sets every week and expects everyone to be an excel expert without teaching it. Doesn't give any feedback and has super high expectations for exams. Does not do a good job explaining the material and often rushes through topics. He's super smart but should not be teaching intro b-stats

Dr. Persaud is very caring and easily accessible outside of class. The class is very interesting but is harder to follow for non-econ majors who have less econ knowledge. You gotta attend all the lectures and take notes. The assigned articles and textbooks will not help a lot. There's no final exam, but a final project and that has been very fun
